about.title: Manteca Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Manteca sits where SR-120 and SR-99 meet, and a lot of daily driving in town funnels through those two highways, along with Yosemite Avenue and Main Street. Public records for 2025 show 283 injury collisions in the city, with 411 people hurt and 2 lives lost. Reports cluster on Friday evenings, roughly 5 p.m. to 7 p.m., when the workweek lets out and traffic thickens. If one of those crashes involved you, the weeks that follow can feel disorienting: adjusters calling, repair estimates piling up, and a body that hurts more on day three than it did at the scene. LawProactive is a free service that connects Manteca residents with an independent personal injury attorney who handles car accident claims in San Joaquin County. We are not a law firm. The attorney you are matched with works on contingency, so there is no fee unless your claim recovers money. Our job is simply to get you talking with someone qualified quickly, before evidence fades and before an insurer locks you into a story.

whyChoose.title: Why Manteca Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Deadlines Are Shorter Than Many People Think
items.desc: California gives you two years to file most car accident claims, but if a city, county, or state agency is involved, that window can shrink to six months. An early connection with an attorney keeps those dates from sneaking up on you.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't Close the Door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even a driver who shares some blame can still recover, with the amount reduced by their percentage. There is also no cap on non-economic damages like pain and lost quality of life.

items.title: No Upfront Cost, and No Recorded Statement Pressure
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. Before you speak with the other driver's insurer on a recorded line, you can have someone in your corner who understands how those calls are used.

items.question: My crash happened on SR-120 near the SR-99 interchange. Does that change anything?
items.answer: It might. Both routes are state highways, and if a roadway condition, signage, or a state vehicle contributed to the collision, a claim against a government entity could be part of the picture. Those claims often carry a six-month notice deadline instead of the usual two years, so it's worth having an attorney review the details early.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are generally not required to give the other insurer a recorded statement, and it's wise to hold off until you've spoken with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can later be used to shrink or deny your claim. A brief, polite decline is enough while you get advice.

items.question: What should I save after a car accident in Manteca?
items.answer: Photos of the vehicles, the roadway, and your injuries are a good start, along with the police report number and the names of any witnesses. Keep every medical record, bill, and pharmacy receipt, and jot down how you feel each day, because symptoms often show up later. If a nearby business may have camera footage, note its location quickly since recordings are frequently overwritten.
